result.topic_en: A planned proof that a homogeneous polynomial admitting a multiplication theorem via bilinear forms must be a determinant after linear substitution, followed by a study of the potential given by the real part of the square root of log z and its boundedness on a domain in the z-plane.
result.transcription:
79.
Suche zu beweisen, dass wenn eine ganze
{+homogene+} rationale Function $f(x, y)\dots$ ein Multiplika-
tionstheorem besitzt, d.h.
$f(x, y)\dots f(x', y')\dots = f(u, v\dots)$
wo $u, v, \dots$ bilineare Verbindungen der $x, y\dots$
$x', y'\dots$ sind, dann nothwendig $f$ durch Ein-
führung geeigneter linearer [-Functe-] Combinatio-
nen eine Determinante wird.

Betrachte das Potential $u =$ reeller Bestand-
theil von $\sqrt{l(z)}$. Auf der nebenstehenden Be-

endlich und stetig, wie erstens die folgende

$u = $ reell. Best. $(i\sqrt{l(\frac{1}{z})})$

items.english: Try to prove that if an integral homogeneous rational function f(x, y)... possesses a multiplication theorem, i.e. f(x, y)... f(x', y')... = f(u, v...) where u, v, ... are bilinear combinations of the x, y... x', y'..., then necessarily f becomes a determinant through the introduction of suitable linear combinations.
